new_statements.quote: 1.2.3 Acento. Dentro de los idiomas Mayas hay tres sistemas diferentes de acentuación (Kaufman, este volumen) y dentro del Mam se encuentran los tres. En Tacaná, el acento cae en la última sílaba, con la excepción de algunos enclíticos que nunca llevan acento (Munson 1984). Ejemplos: ub'éch 'flor', wiinqí'n 'veinte', yaají 'después', tx'eemb'eén 'la cortada'; pero no en enclítico: twaakaáx-a 'tu ganado'. [...] [p.226] En Tacaná no hay ninguna relación entre vocal larga y acento — puede haber más de una vocal larga en la palabra y una vocal larga no necesariamente tiene acento. Sólo lo tiene si también es la última vocal.
new_statements.translation: 1.2.3 Stress. Among the Mayan languages there are three different stress systems (Kaufman, this volume) and all three are found within Mam. In Tacaná, stress falls on the last syllable, with the exception of some enclitics that never bear stress (Munson 1984). Examples: ub'éch 'flower', wiinqí'n 'twenty', yaají 'afterwards', tx'eemb'eén 'the cut'; but not on an enclitic: twaakaáx-a 'your cattle'. [...] In Tacaná there is no relation at all between long vowel and stress — there can be more than one long vowel in the word and a long vowel does not necessarily bear stress. It bears it only if it is also the last vowel.
new_statements.citation: England, Nora C. 1990. El Mam: semejanzas y diferencias regionales. In Nora C. England & Stephen R. Elliott (comps.), Lecturas sobre la lingüística maya, 221-252. La Antigua Guatemala: Centro de Investigaciones Regionales de Mesoamérica (CIRMA) / South Woodstock, VT: Plumsock Mesoamerican Studies.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress in Tacaná (Western) Mam is fixed on the final syllable of the word, insensitive to vowel length (long vowels occur freely in unstressed syllables); certain enclitics (and, per Godfrey 1990 n.9, certain suffixes) fall outside the stress domain, so stress is final in the word excluding enclitics. Corroborated first-hand by Godfrey 1990:300 n.9 ('El acento tiende a estar en la última sílaba, no incluyendo enclíticos y ciertos sufijos') and by Kaufman 1990:67 (Tipo D 'acentúa la última vocal de cada palabra.. Mam Occidental (=Takaneko)').
new_statements.secondary_stress: Nothing said about secondary stress in England 1990, Godfrey 1990 or Kaufman 1990.
new_statements.exceptions: Some enclitics never bear stress (England 1990:225, e.g. twaakaáx-a); Godfrey 1990:300 n.9 adds 'ciertos sufijos' and hedges with 'tiende a'; Kaufman 1990:67: clitics unstressed, rule holds for native vocabulary.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level rule stated on citation forms; enclitics are excluded from the stress domain (stress = last syllable of the host word). England's Tacaná data are credited to Linda Munson's 1984 UCSD dissertation (acknowledgments p.252), so England 1990 is a specialist's comparative statement resting on Munson's primary description; Godfrey 1990 n.9 is an independent first-hand fieldworker's statement (Tacaná 1978-80).
new_statements.identity_note: taca1258 'Tacanec' is a Glottolog bookkeeping entry for retired ISO 639-3 [mtz] (Ethnologue 15: 'Tacaná Mam, Western Mam, Tiló, Mamé'; rural areas west of Tacaná plus Sibinal and Tectitán, San Marcos Dept., Guatemala, and adjacent eastern Chiapas, Mexico), merged into Mam [mam] = Glottolog mamm1241 by CR 2008-055 (2009). The quoted sources describe exactly this variety: England 1990's 'Tacaná' column (data from Munson 1984, 'Western Mam'), Godfrey 1990's 'Mam de Tacaná, Takaneko' (fieldwork in Tacaná town 1978-80), Kaufman 1990's 'Mam Occidental (=Takaneko)', and Godfrey & Collins 1987's 'Mam tacaneco' group (Tacaná + Sibinal). Note the stress rule differs from the catalog's mamm1241 entry (England 1975/1983, Ixtahuacán = Northern Mam, weight-sensitive) and from Southern Mam (penultimate); Western/Tacaná Mam is fixed final. Not to be confused with Tektiteko (tekt1235, Tectitán; also final stress per Stevenson 1987) or with Takanan 'Tacana' (taca1256, Bolivia).

sources.note: ch.5 'Tacaná, SM (51 y 52)', printed p.99 (PDF p.131): Tacaneco is the Mam dialect most like Tectiteco and most different from the rest; 'En el plano fonológico, son muy comunes las vocales prolongadas en las sílabas no acentuadas. En las demás variantes, las vocales prolongadas tienden a aparecer solamente en las sílabas tónicas.' No explicit stress-position rule; ch.6 p.111 defines the 'Mam tacaneco' group = Tacaná + Sibinal (+ adjacent Chiapas). Appendix 6 gives stress-marked phonetic transcriptions of the 80 test sentences for Tacaná points 51-53 (not transcribed here).
